items.title: Early hemodynamic and metabolic changes following extracorporeal hemadsorption in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock: A retrospective, single-center observational cohort study.
items.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains associated with high mortality. We investigated early hemodynamic and metabolic changes following adjunctive extracorporeal hemadsorption in a real-world AMI-CS cohort. This retrospective single-center landmark analysis included adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with AMI-CS classified as Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stage C or higher between January 2017 and July 2025. Patients who died within 24 h of ICU admission were excluded; among patients receiving hemadsorption, only those treated for at least 24 h were included. Propensity score matching was performed using sex, prior cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), admission lactate, admission vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), and admission Horovitz index. The principal analysis compared pretreatment values with those at 24 h after treatment initiation; corresponding pseudo-timepoints were assigned in matched controls. Serial assessments at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h characterized VIS and lactate trajectories. Of 479 screened patients with AMI-CS, 398 met eligibility criteria for the 24-h landmark analysis, including 57 treated with adjunctive hemadsorption and 341 controls. Propensity score matching yielded 35 matched pairs and improved balance across the prespecified covariates, although residual imbalance persisted for prior CPR, CRRT, admission lactate, and admission VIS. In the matched cohort, hemadsorption-treated patients showed early within-group reductions in VIS (56.2 to 23.0; P =0.009) and lactate (2.0 to 1.5 mmol/L; P P =0.031) and lactate dehydrogenase ( P =0.018). In matched controls, lactate likewise decreased significantly, whereas VIS remained unchanged, and tissue-injury markers did not show a comparable early decline. Although VIS and lactate improved over time overall, no significant time-by-treatment interaction was observed over 48 h for VIS ( P =0.834) or lactate ( P =0.427). Exploratory subgroup and multivariable analyses revealed no evidence of a differential mortality benefit. In-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between matched groups (45.7% vs. 42.9%; log-rank P =0.909), and hemadsorption was not independently associated with mortality (odds ratio=1.05, 95% CI: 0.36-3.08; P =0.934). In this exploratory propensity score-matched landmark analysis of AMI-CS, hemadsorption-treated patients showed early within-group hemodynamic and metabolic changes, but subsequent VIS and lactate trajectories did not differ significantly from matched controls, and in-hospital survival was not improved. Residual imbalance and the observational design limit causal interpretation. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

items.title: Bioengineering platforms for precision respiratory rehabilitation: biomaterials, lung-mimetic models, and wearable biointerfaces.
items.abstract: Pulmonary rehabilitation is an established intervention for chronic respiratory diseases, but heterogeneous responses, limited mechanistic resolution, and incomplete real-world monitoring restrict precision delivery. Bioengineering platforms may address these gaps by linking clinically actionable respiratory traits to biomaterials, lung-mimetic models, and wearable biointerfaces. This critical narrative Review examines how bioengineering platforms may address three complementary translational needs in precision respiratory rehabilitation: modulation of recovery-relevant pulmonary microenvironments, mechanistic and safety testing in human-relevant lung models, and continuous measurement of rehabilitation exposure and response. We organize these functions within a Trait-Material-Interface-Endpoint framework that links engineering-actionable traits to appropriate platforms, validation requirements, and patient-centred outcomes. The evidence base is uneven. Clinical benefits of pulmonary rehabilitation are well established, whereas direct evidence that biomaterials enhance rehabilitation outcomes remains limited, and many organ-on-chip and wearable applications are still at preclinical or validation stages. These technologies should therefore complement rather than replace guideline-based rehabilitation. Future studies should use staged safety testing, trait-based enrolment, validated digital measures, patient-centred functional outcomes, and implementation endpoints to determine whether bioengineering can make respiratory rehabilitation more measurable, personalized, and clinically translatable.

items.title: Intravascular lithotripsy vs. rotational atherectomy for severely calcified coronary lesions with concomitant tortuosity or angulation: a propensity-weighted real-world study from China.
items.abstract: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an emerging technique for the treatment of severely calcified coronary lesions, yet head-to-head evidence comparing its prognostic value against standard rotational atherectomy (RA) in real-world practice, particularly in patients with tortuous or angulated coronary anatomy, remains lacking. This retrospective observational cohort study included 247 patients with severely calcified coronary lesions and concomitant tortuous or angulated anatomy who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2023 and March 2025, comprising 137 patients treated with RA and 110 treated with IVL. The primary endpoint was one-year composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), encompassing all-cause mortality, target vessel revascularization, heart failure rehospitalization, in-stent restenosis, and stroke. Three complementary analytical strategies of escalating robustness, multivariable logistic regression, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) using a gradient boosted model (GBM), and doubly robust estimation, were employed to estimate the treatment effect of IVL vs. RA. Covariate balance was assessed using standardized mean differences (SMD ≤ 0.10). Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable between groups, with significant differences observed only in LDL-C, total cholesterol, and HDL-C (all P   P   P  = 0.14) and doubly robust estimation (OR 0.48, 0.18-1.25; P  = 0.13). Among secondary outcomes, one-year heart failure rehospitalization was significantly lower with IVL (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.03-0.78; P  = 0.03); no significant differences were observed for mortality, target vessel revascularization, stroke, or in-stent restenosis. In this retrospective cohort of patients with severely calcified coronary lesions, all of whom had concomitant tortuous or angulated anatomy, IVL was associated with a lower risk of one-year MACE compared with RA, an effect driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalisation. The consistency across three analytical models suggests robustness of this finding, although confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials is warranted.

items.title: Surgical Decision-Making in Staphylococcus aureus Infective Endocarditis With Structural Valve Destruction Despite the Absence of Overt Heart Failure: The Role of the Endocarditis Team.
items.abstract: In young patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia, early transoesophageal echocardiography plays a pivotal role in the detection of destructive infective endocarditis and promotes timely surgical management.

items.title: Lifestyle associations with hypertension and diabetes risk via metabolic function and physical indicators: a cross-sectional serial mediation model among community adults.
items.abstract: To examine whether lifestyle is associated with hypertension and diabetes risk via sequential indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators among community adults. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6,178 community adults in Nanning, southern China. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to examine the direct and indirect associations among lifestyle, metabolic function, physical indicators, and disease risk. Bias-corrected bootstrap analyses with 5,000 resamples were performed to evaluate indirect associations. The model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.917, RMSEA = 0.048); the chi-square/df ratio (5.19) was elevated, as is common in samples of this size. Physical indicators exhibited the strongest direct association with disease risk ( β  = 0.763, P   β  = 0.048, P  = 0.010). Healthy lifestyle was associated with lower disease risk via indirect pathways involving physical indicators alone ( β  = -0.360, P  = 0.001) and via the sequential indirect pathway involving metabolic function and physical indicators ( β  = -0.011, P  = 0.021). For unhealthy lifestyle, indirect associations with higher disease risk were observed via metabolic function ( β  = 0.003, P  = 0.036) and physical indicators ( β  = 0.092, P  = 0.014), whereas the sequential indirect pathway was not statistically significant ( P  = 0.104). Direct associations of lifestyle with disease risk were small in magnitude (| β | ≤ 0.035) and of limited clinical importance; only the direct association of unhealthy lifestyle reached statistical significance ( β  = -0.035, P  = 0.013). In this cross-sectional sample, lifestyle was associated with hypertension and diabetes risk primarily via indirect pathways involving metabolic function and physical indicators. These findings should be interpreted as correlational and cannot establish causality. They highlight the importance of integrated lifestyle management and early metabolic risk assessment for the prevention of hypertension and diabetes in community settings.

items.title: Case Report: Multimodal treatment of pediatric H3G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma: a safety and feasibility case report combining precision medicine and tumor treating fields with conventional care.
items.abstract: Diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3G34-mutant (H3G34-DHG) is a rare, highly malignant brain tumour with a dismal prognosis and a median time to progression (TTP) of 10 months with best available practice. We report a case of a 13-year-old boy with H3G34-DHG who underwent a multimodal treatment strategy, combining backbone chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, tumour treating fields with Wilms Tumour-1 (WT1) directed dendritic cell immunotherapy and targeted therapy (STAT3-inhibition). The patient had a TTP of 787 days or 25 months, more than double the literature-reported median, with preserved quality of life and showing downregulation of WT1. This case supports the feasibility of combining multiple therapeutic modalities in the management of high-risk paediatric brain tumours, with potential synergy between different treatment elements. While access to novel therapies in the context of clinical trials remains essential, this case illustrates how treatment can be tailored to individual tumour biology and tolerability. The rationale presented in this detailed case report can inform future trial designs and promote precision medicine approaches for this tumour type.

items.title: Clinical phenotype and diagnostic pathways of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in a Ukrainian cohort.
items.abstract: Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a common multisystem genomic disorder with marked phenotypic variability and diagnostic delay. Data on diagnostic pathways and specialist involvement in Eastern Europe remain limited. We aimed to characterize diagnostic pathways and clinical triggers, assess specialist involvement and follow-up, and identify factors associated with diagnosis before or after 1 year of age in a Ukrainian cohort. We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of patients with 22q11.2DS registered in the Ukrainian National Registry of Primary Immunodeficiencies. Clinical manifestations, diagnostic triggers, specialists involved in diagnosis and follow-up, immunological findings, and age at diagnosis were analyzed. The cohort included 126 patients, with a median age of 12 years (range, 0.1-39 years) and median age at diagnosis of 1.0 year (range, 0.1-18 years). Among 120 patients with available diagnostic timing, 63 (52.5%) were diagnosed within the first year, including the two antenatal cases. Congenital heart disease (CHD) was the most frequent major manifestation (74/89, 83.1%), followed by craniofacial dysmorphism (62/74, 83.8%), thymic hypoplasia (54/65, 83.1%), developmental delay (46/62, 74.2%), and recurrent infections (44/65, 67.7%). Among 83 patients with documented diagnostic triggers, CHD was the most frequent (61/83, 73.5%). Developmental delay was more frequent among patients diagnosed after 1 year than within the first year (22.9% vs. 4.4%, p  = 0.0135). Immunodeficiency was a diagnostic trigger in 10/83 patients (12.0%), despite T-cell lymphopenia in 31/59 (52.5%). Immunologists and geneticists were most frequently involved in diagnosis. Cardiothoracic surgeons and cardiologists were more frequently involved among patients diagnosed within the first year than after 1 year (27.9% vs. 9.1%, p  = 0.0411). Among 13 patients diagnosed after implementation of TREC/KREC newborn screening, two were identified following an abnormal screening result. In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve timely diagnosis of 22q11.2DS in Ukraine.

items.title: Podocarpusflavone A sensitizes MASLD-related hepatocellular carcinoma to lenvatinib by targeting ABAT and ALDH2.
items.abstract: Despite the rising global incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-related hepatocellular carcinoma (MASLD-HCC), immunotherapy offers limited survival benefits in this non-viral etiology, positioning lenvatinib as a critical treatment that necessitates novel strategies to enhance its efficacy. This study aimed to identify MASLD-HCC signature genes and to explore a novel agent to overcome lenvatinib resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified signature genes, validated by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, Western blot, and spatial transcriptomics in human and murine specimens. Virtual screening identified a natural compound targeting hub genes. Direct binding was confirmed using molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and surface plasmon resonance. Therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms were comprehensively evaluated in vitro under lipotoxic stress conditions and in vivo using diet-induced orthotopic MASLD-HCC mouse models. A 170-gene signature was established, with ABAT and ALDH2 prioritized as hub genes. Podocarpusflavone A (PCFA) emerged as a dual-targeting agent that robustly reverses acquired lenvatinib resistance. Instead of increasing protein abundance, PCFA directly binds these targets, which is accompanied by markedly enhanced cellular ABAT and ALDH activities. This diminishes the protective GABA shield and disrupts the mitochondrial NAD⁺ balance, precipitating a lethal mitochondrial superoxide burst and inhibiting key oncogenic pathways. In vivo, the PCFA and lenvatinib combination profoundly suppressed orthotopic tumor progression and was associated with short-term improvements in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis-related histological findings, with no evident toxicity under the conditions tested. PCFA combined with lenvatinib represents a promising strategy for MASLD-HCC and provides mechanistic insights into its antitumor activity.

items.title: Targeting the Lactate-Lactylation Axis in Cancer Immunotherapy Resistance: From Tumor Acidosis to Context-Dependent Immune Reprogramming.
items.abstract: Lactate is now recognized as an active immunometabolic regulator in the tumor microenvironment (TME), not simply as a glycolytic byproduct. Its immunological effects arise through several related but distinct routes. Extracellular acidosis, glucose competition, and impaired monocarboxylate transporter-dependent flux can impair CD8 + T cells, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Lactate- and proton-sensing receptors can also favor suppressive myeloid and regulatory-cell programs. Histone and non-histone lactylation add another layer by linking lactate availability to chromatin regulation and protein function. During sustained or repeated metabolic stress, these processes may support regulatory T-cell fitness, suppressive programs in tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, checkpoint expression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Lactylation is a plausible mediator through which sustained metabolic stress may be converted into persistent immune reprogramming; however, post-withdrawal persistence and cellular memory remain to be demonstrated in cancer. We distinguish lactate-dependent regulation from acidosis and evaluate the links to immune dysfunction and treatment resistance by their temporal, causal, and clinical support. This framework defines tests of post-exposure persistence and connects mechanistic evidence and pharmacological specificity to biomarker development and mechanism-matched trial design.

items.title: Immune potentiating effects of the HDAC inhibitor Zabadinostat on human immune and tumor cells.
items.abstract: The use of histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACis) to reverse epigenetic silencing of immune-associated genes has shown clinical efficacy in hematologic malignancies but not solid tumors. Here we explored the transcriptional and phenotypic effects of in vitro exposures of Zabadinostat, a second-generation class I HDACi, on human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and solid tumor cells to support its combination with immunotherapy. Zabadinostat induced activation of CD8 + and CD4 + T cells and natural killer cells, while reducing the frequency and suppressive function of regulatory T cells. Increases in stem-like memory T cells, a rare subset of multipotent, self-renewing cells important for anti-tumor control, were also observed, and these immune effects coincided with increased expression of transcriptional activation marks H3K9ac and H3K27ac. Zabadinostat increased PD-L1, FAS, ICAM-1, and HLA expression in tumor cells and reverted epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related proteins. These data show that Zabadinostat is a novel immunomodulatory agent with multifaceted effects, capable of enhancing immune effector function, reducing immunosuppression, and improving the visibility of tumor cells to immune-mediated attack. These findings support the use of Zabadinostat in combination with immunotherapeutic agents.

items.title: Liver transplantation outcomes, systemic immune-inflammatory phenotype, and predictors of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence in an HBV/HDV-endemic region: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B and D virus (HBV/HDV) coinfection sustains a hepatic inflammatory microenvironment from which hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises. Although advances in liver transplantation have improved survival, HCC recurrence remains a major challenge affecting long-term outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate post-transplant outcomes and identify risk factors associated with HCC recurrence among liver transplant recipients in Mongolia, and to characterize their pre-transplant systemic immune-inflammatory phenotype. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 146 patients with HCC who underwent liver transplantation at the National Cancer Center of Mongolia from 2018 through February 2026. Survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test, and factors associated with HCC recurrence were assessed using univariable Cox regression. Pre-transplant neutrophil (ANC) and lymphocyte (ALC) counts and their ratio (NLR) were available for 139 recipients; lymphopenia was an ALC below 1.0 ×10 9 /L. The 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival rates were 88.7%, 82.1%, and 80.5%, respectively, with no significant difference between patients within versus beyond the Milan criteria (p = 0.097). HCC recurrence occurred in 3.4% of recipients and was significantly more common among patients beyond the Milan criteria (p = 0.001). Macrovascular invasion (HR, 12.76; p = 0.005), beyond-Milan status (HR, 10.04; p = 0.039), higher Edmondson-Steiner grade (HR, 9.25; p = 0.047), and elevated AFP (HR, 15.95; p = 0.003) were associated with recurrence in univariate analysis. HCV/HBV/HDV coinfection was significantly associated with higher post-transplant mortality. Median NLR was 1.84 and 39.6% of recipients were lymphopenic; NLR varied inversely with the ALC (ρ = -0.61) and positively with the ANC (ρ = +0.67, both p < 0.001). Lymphopenia increased with tumor burden (34.4% within Milan, 51.2% beyond, 3 of 5 recurrences), NLR was higher when HCC was histologically confirmed on the explant (2.10 vs 1.44, p = 0.015), and recurrence deaths showed the highest NLR with the lowest ALC, rejection deaths the reverse. Liver transplantation achieved favorable survival outcomes in patients with HCC in Mongolia. In exploratory univariate analysis, incorporating pre-transplant tumor characteristics, biomarkers, and viral etiology, together with the pre-transplant lymphocyte compartment, may improve prediction of recurrence and post-transplant mortality, particularly among patients beyond the Milan criteria.

items.title: Circulating CXCR6+PD-1+ CD8 T cells are associated with liver inflammation and disease severity in hepatitis flares.
items.abstract: Marked hepatitis flares, defined in this study as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevations exceeding five times the upper limit of normal, occur in acute and chronic liver diseases and may be associated with severe liver injury. However, the circulating immune profiles associated with the extent of liver injury remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize circulating CD8 T cell phenotypes and soluble immune mediators during hepatitis flares across different etiologies. In a retrospective cross-sectional analysis, soluble immune mediators and circulating CD8 T cell phenotypes were analyzed in 71 patients with hepatitis flares using Luminex assays and spectral flow cytometry. Exploratory functional experiments included in vitro PBMC stimulation and co-culture of sorted CD8 T cell subsets with Huh7 hepatoma cells. A public HBV single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset was reanalyzed to contextualize circulating and intrahepatic CD8 T cell states. Circulating CXCR6+PD-1+ CD8 T cell frequencies were associated with biochemical markers of liver injury and dysfunction. HLA-DR expression within this subset was associated with the hepatocyte injury index, bilirubin levels, and plasma CXCL10 (IP-10) concentrations. Activation-marker and granzyme expression differed across flare etiologies, and CXCR6+PD-1+ CD8 T cells retained inducible effector responses following cytokine stimulation. Reanalysis of a public HBV scRNA-seq dataset identified a liver-enriched CXCR6/PDCD1/HLA-DRAhi GZMKhi CD8 T cell state. Circulating CXCR6+PD-1+ CD8 T cells represent an activation-associated population that correlates with biochemical liver injury during hepatitis flares and retains inducible effector capacity. Whether these cells contribute to or reflect ongoing liver inflammation remains to be determined.

items.title: Incidence of liver cancer and decompensated cirrhosis amongst hepatitis B and C notifications in Tasmania- a data linkage study.
items.abstract: Liver cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related death globally, with both incidence and mortality rates rising sharply in Australia over the past three decades. Chronic hepatitis B and C are major contributors to liver cancer, and its common precursor, decompensated cirrhosis. This study assessed the incidence of liver cancer and decompensated cirrhosis among individuals with hepatitis B and C in Tasmania. A retrospective population-based study was conducted using linked datasets. The cohort included all individuals with a notification for hepatitis B and/or C in Tasmania from 1995 to 2022. Cases were linked to the Tasmanian Cancer Register and admitted patient data from Tasmanian public hospitals. Incidence rates per 1,000 person-years were calculated for liver cancer and decompensated cirrhosis. Between 1995 and 2022, 1,280 hepatitis B (55.5% male) and 6,658 hepatitis C (64.3% male) notifications were recorded in Tasmania. A total of 145 liver cancer registrations and 270 decompensated cirrhosis-related admissions were observed. Among individuals with hepatitis B, the incidence rates were 5.39 per 1,000 person-years for liver cancer and 3.00 per 1,000 person-years for decompensated cirrhosis. Among those with hepatitis C, corresponding rates were 2.33 and 5.02 per 1,000 person-years. While the number of liver-related outcomes was relatively low and did not support more detailed analyses, a trend towards higher incidence rates was observed over the study period. These findings highlight the burden of liver-related complications among individuals with hepatitis B and C in Tasmania. Liver cancer was more common among those with hepatitis B, while decompensated cirrhosis was more frequent among those with hepatitis C. Observed trends should be interpreted cautiously, as they may reflect changes in population characteristics, surveillance, and healthcare engagement. Strengthening testing, treatment uptake, and long-term monitoring is essential to reduce the burden of advanced liver disease in this regional setting.

items.title: In Silico affinity profiling differentiates consensus vaccine sequences where genetic and structural similarity fail: a case study on HCV E2 genotypic and pan-genotypic antigens.
items.abstract: The World Health Organization's goal to eradicate hepatitis C by 2030 remains unattainable without an effective vaccine. Consensus generation combined with layering has the potential to introduce vaccines against highly variable viruses like HCV. However, this approach yields numerous candidates that require in vivo testing. Profiling the affinity of these candidates to monoclonal antibodies via in silico methods can help reduce the number of candidates. In this study, we evaluated the differentiating power of in silico affinity profiling on two previously reported genotypic consensus sequences (NOTC1 and NOTC2) and two newly generated pan-genotypic sequences (L1-CON and L2-CON), each derived using distinct consensus generation algorithms. Structural models of these sequences were generated via homology modelling and simulated within a canonical ensemble. The resulting average structures were then used as inputs for antigen-antibody docking studies against all reported antibody structures known to bind to each epitope in the HCV E2 protein. Docking results for epitope II revealed lower binding energies for NOTC1 compared to NOTC2 (p = 0279) and J-2a (p = 0.0132) consistent with their reported in vivo performance. This discrimination was not reproduced in genetic distance from the common ancestor of Genotype 1 and also structural similarity between protein models and crystalographed antigen. Notably, neither sequence nor structural similarity correlated with the docking outcomes, highlighting the predictive value of the proposed affinity profiling pipeline as an initial assessment tool for vaccine candidates.

items.title: Identification of coding-region mutations associated with attenuation of an Egyptian duck hepatitis A virus type 1 isolate following serial egg passage.
items.abstract: Duck hepatitis A virus type 1 (DHAV-1) causes a highly contagious disease with high mortality in young ducklings. Although serial passage in embryonated eggs is widely used for virus adaptation and attenuation, the molecular changes associated with DHAV-1 attenuation remain poorly understood. A virulent Egyptian DHAV-1 isolate was serially passaged 84 times in embryonated chicken eggs. The parental virus (P0) and the passage-84 virus (P84) were subsequently compared for pathogenicity in Pekin ducklings, replication in embryonated chicken eggs, and whole-genome sequence analysis. The parental virus caused 100% mortality within 72 h, whereas the P84 virus caused neither clinical signs nor mortality and replicated to higher titers in embryonated chicken eggs, demonstrating complete attenuation. Whole-genome sequencing identified 11 nucleotide substitutions, including four non-synonymous mutations in the VP3, 2A, and 2C proteins. Serial passage in embryonated chicken eggs resulted in complete attenuation of DHAV-1 after 84 passages, despite the accumulation of four amino acid substitutions. These findings demonstrate that profound phenotypic attenuation can arise with minimal genomic evolution and identify candidate mutations in VP3, 2A, and particularly 2C for future reverse-genetics studies and rational live vaccine development.

items.title: From T-cell renewal to immune longevity: a multilevel capacity framework for immune aging.
items.abstract: Consider what the T-cell compartment accomplishes. For decades it sustains immune competence while the thymus shrinks, antigens accumulate, and tissues change around it. We propose that this longevity rests on four coupled capacities: input renewal, repertoire maintenance and clonal dynamics, lineage-constrained plasticity, and tissue-contextual fitness. Input renewal is treated as a proxy domain inferred from calibrated peripheral correlates, not as a direct measure of thymic flux. Our claim is simple: these capacities need not age in concert, whether one compares individuals, tissues, or challenges. The biology behind them is well known. Thymic involution restricts the entry of naive T cells, antigen history reshapes the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, metabolic and epigenetic changes erode proliferative reserve, and aged tissue niches alter survival, trafficking, and local function. Nevertheless, some individuals retain protective responses in particular subsets and tissues, a pattern consistent with compensation during aging and exceptional longevity. We introduce renewable potential as a broader concept than T-cell stemness and distinguish terminal differentiation from exhaustion and senescence-like phenotypes. We then consider how longitudinal turnover measurements, clone-aware analyses, and perturbation studies can move the field beyond cross-sectional, age-associated signatures. Its predictions are concrete: capacities may disagree within a person, compartments may age at different rates, the limiting capacity may depend on context, compensation may give way to maladaptive fixation, and intervention responses may vary with the baseline capacity profile. Vaccination and infection, cancer, transplantation, autoimmunity, and tissue inflammation illustrate these constraints. On this view, the T-cell immune-longevity capacity profile describes a context-dependent pattern of deficits and compensations, not a universal immune-age score or a proxy for chronological age.

items.title: Stage-Dependent Roles of PANoptosis in MASLD: From Isolated Steatosis to Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: PANoptosis is an inflammatory form of programmed cell death mediated by PANoptosome complexes that integrate the key features of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis. Although PANoptosis has been increasingly implicated in liver injury, inflammation, and tumor immunity, its stage-dependent roles across the full spectrum of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), from isolated steatosis to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), remain incompletely defined. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms of PANoptosis and discusses its dynamic evolution during MASLD progression. In isolated steatosis, PANoptosis-related signaling may remain in a sublethal activation state, contributing to early stress responses without extensive inflammatory cell death. During progression to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver fibrosis, metabolic, immune, and structural insults may synergistically amplify PANoptosis-related inflammatory cell death, thereby promoting hepatocyte injury, inflammatory amplification, and fibrogenesis. In HCC, PANoptosis may exert context-dependent dual effects: acute and robust activation in tumor cells may enhance immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity, whereas chronic or excessive activation in the liver microenvironment may sustain inflammation, immune suppression, and tumor progression. These stage-specific features suggest that PANoptosis-related molecules may serve as candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets for MASLD stratification and precision treatment. Rather than simply inhibiting or inducing PANoptosis, future strategies should aim to modulate the intensity, duration, and cellular specificity of PANoptosis activation. By integrating mechanistic evidence with translational perspectives, this review proposes a stage-dependent framework for understanding PANoptosis in the MASLD-HCC continuum.

items.title: Preoperative Biliary Drainage for Pancreatobiliary Tumor.
items.abstract: Obstructive jaundice from pancreatobiliary tumors causes bacterial translocation into the liver and systemic circulation, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, multiorgan failure, and malnutrition, thereby increasing perioperative risk. Preoperative biliary drainage (PBD) aims to reverse these effects and enable safer neoadjuvant therapy and surgery. However, whether the benefits of relieving obstructive jaundice outweigh the risks of procedure-related and perioperative infectious complications remains controversial. This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of the indications, modalities, timing, and ongoing debates regarding PBD in patients with distal and hilar biliary malignancies. In general, indications for PBD include cholangitis, severe or progressive jaundice with organ dysfunction, the need to optimize liver function for neoadjuvant therapy, and anticipated prolonged preoperative delays. In patients undergoing major hepatectomy, future liver remnant protection warrants additional consideration. Endoscopic biliary drainage is generally preferred over percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage (PTBD) because PTBD carries a potential oncological risk and causes patient discomfort. However, PTBD remains an alternative to endoscopic drainage or as a supplementary method to drain additional effective liver volume. Fully covered self-expandable metal stents offer superior patency during the preoperative period but may increase the risks of pancreatitis, cholecystitis, and local inflammation, potentially affecting surgical complexity. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biliary drainage shows promise but requires further validation of its safety profile and long-term oncologic outcomes. Given its distinct benefits and risks, PBD should be tailored to the patient's clinical status, treatment plan, and institutional expertise. Further studies are needed to evaluate the optimal timing of surgery, the ideal stent design, and the impact of each PBD modality on perioperative safety and long-term oncologic outcomes.

items.title: Cancer-associated fibroblast-derived lactate drives cholangiocarcinoma progression via H4K12la-mediated oxidative phosphorylation activation.
items.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy, and chemoresistance is a major cause of poor prognosis. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving CCA progression from a tumor microenvironment perspective and to develop novel strategies to enhance chemosensitivity. Single-cell RNA-seq, untargeted metabolomics, and proteomics were used to identify the source of lactate in the CCA microenvironment and the metabolic reprogramming of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To evaluate the impact of CAF-derived lactate on prognosis, we performed AAV-mediated MCT4 knockdown followed by hydrodynamic injection to induce a CCA model. Co-culture models were combined with genome-wide CUT&Tag, MeRIP-seq, and RIP-seq to resolve epigenetic and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. The antitumor effects of 7ACC1 (a small molecule reported to inhibit lactate uptake), alone or in combination with gemcitabine, were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic liver xenograft models. CAFs undergo glycolytic reprogramming, resulting in aberrant lactate accumulation. Mechanistically, CAF-derived lactate induces H4K12 lactylation (H4K12la) in CCA cells, which in turn activates the IGF2BP3/ATF3 axis to upregulate oxidative phosphorylation and promote tumor progression. The lactate shuttle inhibitor 7ACC1, combined with gemcitabine, exerts promising antitumor effects. Clinically, high levels of MCT4, α SMA, and H4K12la are associated with poor prognosis in patients with CCA. These findings reveal that CAFs drive CCA progression via lactate-induced H4K12la, which activates the IGF2BP3/ATF3 axis. The findings provide a preclinical rationale for further evaluation of lactate-uptake-targeting strategies in combination with gemcitabine for CCA.
